intended_object: For a binary-outcome network model on a pair-source graph, this is the conditional expectation E[sgn O_v | sources = x] of the ±1 sign of the outcome at vertex v, given the values x of the latent sources. Inferred from the docstring and from how it is used in the moment-factorization lemma in CycleObstruction.lean.
explanation:
In `GModel`, `resp v c` is the probability that the outcome at v is 0 (`false`), given the values c of the sources incident to v. This matches `respMass q b = if b then 1 - q else q`. The library fixes the sign convention `sgn false = 1`, `sgn true = -1`. So E[sgn O_v | x] = q·1 + (1 − q)·(−1) = 2q − 1, with q = `M.resp v (fun e => x e.1)`, and that is exactly what the definition computes.

Restricting the global source assignment x to the edges incident to v is the right input. The library relies on this: `sResp_congr` shows the value depends only on those edges, and the factorization lemma proves Σ_w law(w)·∏_{v∈F} sgn(w v) = Σ_x lat(x)·∏_{v∈F} sResp v x. That is the intended meaning. Its bound in [−1, 1] for valid models is also proved (`sResp_bound`).

The quantity only makes sense inside the library's own `GModel` framework (binary outcomes and finite latent alphabets on a pair-source graph). Mathlib has no general counterpart, so the definition is not too narrow.
